title: Slot-Based Recurrence for Efficient k=3 Birthday Counting
description: Optimizes the k=3 birthday counting formula by replacing the O(d^n) enumeration over all assignments with an O(n²) slot-based recurrence R(n, e, s). The state (e, s) tracks empty and single-occupied day slots; the recurrence R(n+1, e, s) = e·R(n, e−1, s+1) + s·R(n, e, s−1) computes the count in O(n²) operations. Proves the capacity theorem (R=0 when n > 2e+s), the upper bound R(n,e,s) ≤ (e+s)^n, the general formula birthdayCount3 3 d = d³ - d, and verifies k=3 thresholds for d=3,4,5,7,10 and d=365 (n=88) by native_decide. Fully verified: 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

overview.historicalContext: The exact birthday probability requires counting functions f : Fin n → Fin d with all fibers of size ≤ k-1 (for k-way coincidence). For k=3, this is |{f : Fin n → Fin d : all fibers ≤ 2}|. Flajolet and Sedgewick (Analytic Combinatorics, 2009) give exponential generating functions for these counts. The threshold for d=365 days (n=88 for k=3) was computed by Diaconis and Mosteller (1989). The computational challenge is that d^n grows exponentially while the counting problem has only O(n²) degrees of freedom — a gap exploitable by dynamic programming on the day-type state.
overview.problemStatement:
**OQ-01 of birthday-problem-oq-03-oq-01**

*Can the recursive birthday formula be made computationally efficient enough for native_decide verification at d=365?*

The extension-counting framework from the parent file shows that valid (n+1)-assignments extend n-assignments by choosing a non-full day. The efficiency problem: summing over all n-assignments is O(d^n).

**Solution**: Replace individual assignment tracking with slot-state tracking. The state (e, s) captures everything needed for the recurrence:
- e = empty days (each can receive 1 more person)
- s = single days (each can receive exactly 1 more person)

Recurrence: R(n+1, e, s) = e · R(n, e−1, s+1) + s · R(n, e, s−1)

This reduces the computation from O(d^n) to O(n²), making d=365, n=88 tractable.
overview.text: The slot-based recurrence R(n, e, s) computes the exact k=3 birthday count efficiently by tracking day slot states rather than individual assignments. The total count birthdayCount3 n d = R n d 0 satisfies a 3-term recurrence (O(n²) computation) vs the naive O(d^n). Key results: capacity theorem (R=0 beyond 2e+s), polynomial upper bound, and verified thresholds for small d.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Main definition**: R n e s counts ways to place n people into e empty + s single slots.
**Base**: R 0 e s = 1 (nothing to place, one way).
**Step**: R(n+1, e, s) = e·R(n, e−1, s+1) + s·R(n, e, s−1) (place person in empty or single slot).
**Total**: birthdayCount3 n d = R n d 0.
**Capacity**: R=0 when n > 2e+s; proved by induction on n with case analysis on e=0 and s=0.
**Bound**: R n e s ≤ (e+s)^n; proved by induction with Nat case splits to handle subtraction.
keyInsights: **State compression**: instead of tracking n! full assignments, track only (e, s) — the day multiplicity histogram restricted to non-full days
**Reachable state count**: after k people, s + 2c = k (c = full days), so s has at most k/2+1 values — the state space is O(n) not exponential
**Nat subtraction safety**: the Nat subtraction e-1 and s-1 in the recurrence is harmless because 0-coefficient kills the call when e=0 or s=0
**Capacity theorem**: when n > 2e + s, the slots are over-capacity and R = 0 — this is the formal version of the pigeonhole bound from the parent file
**Big-number barrier**: for d=365, n=88, the values are ~10^50 digits, requiring external verification of the threshold axioms

sections.title: Module Header and Imports
sections.summary: File docstring: the slot-based recurrence optimization for counting k=3 birthday assignments, its O(n²) efficiency vs O(d^n) naive enumeration, and the axiom-free status (formerly 2 axioms, eliminated via native_decide).
sections.mathContext: Header only. Defines the problem: count f : Fin n → Fin d with all fibers ≤ 2, tracked via slot state (e empty, s single).

sections.title: Section I: The Slot-Based Recurrence
sections.summary: Defines R n e s (ways to place n people into e empty + s single slots) by recursion on n, and birthdayCount3 n d := R n d 0.
sections.mathContext: R 0 e s = 1; R (n+1) e s = e·R n (e-1) (s+1) + s·R n e (s-1). Nat subtraction is safe because the coefficient kills the call at e=0 or s=0.

sections.title: Section II: Core Recurrence Properties
sections.summary: Simp lemmas R_zero, R_succ, plus the capacity bound: R n e s = 0 when 2e+s < n, and birthdayCount3_over_capacity (count is 0 when 2d < n).
sections.mathContext: R_exceeds_capacity is proved by induction on n, case-splitting e and s to discharge each summand via Nat subtraction arithmetic (omega).

sections.title: Section III: Basic Birthday Count Formulas
sections.summary: Closed forms for small n: birthdayCount3 0 d = 1, 1 d = d, 2 d = d²; decide-checks for n=3 at d=3,4,5,10; and zero-at-limit (count is 0 at n = 2d+1).
sections.mathContext: Base cases by simp/ring on the recurrence; the n=3 small-d values are confirmed by decide as anchors for the general n=3 formula in Section X.

sections.title: Section IV: Bounds on the Count
sections.summary: R n e s ≤ (e+s)^n (count bounded by unconstrained placements) and its corollary birthdayCount3 n d ≤ d^n.
sections.mathContext: R_le_pow by induction on n, case-splitting e and s to handle Nat subtraction (e-1+(s+1) ≤ e+s fails at e=0), then Nat.mul_le_mul_left + pow monotonicity.

sections.title: Section V: Recurrence Unfolding
sections.summary: One- and two-step unfoldings of birthdayCount3 (n+1) and (n+2) exposing the slot transitions.
sections.mathContext: birthdayCount3 (n+1) d = d·R n (d-1) 1; the (n+2) form splits into empty→single and single→full branches.

sections.title: Section VI: Computational Verifications (via decide)
sections.summary: decide-verified counts and threshold inequalities for d=3,4,5 (e.g. threshold_d4_lower/upper bracketing the k=3 half-probability point).
sections.mathContext: Each P(no triple) = birthdayCount3 n d / d^n; the threshold is where 2·(valid count) crosses d^n. Small d is feasible with plain decide.

sections.title: Section VII: The k=3 Birthday Threshold for d=365
sections.summary: The headline result: via native_decide, the exact k=3 threshold for d=365 is n=88 (2·birthdayCount3 88 365 < 365^88 ≤ 2·birthdayCount3 87 365).
sections.mathContext: native_decide runs the O(88²)≈7744-evaluation slot recurrence over ~200-digit integers using GMP-backed compiled evaluation; the naive d^88 enumeration is infeasible.

sections.title: Section VIII: Efficiency Analysis
sections.summary: State-space bounds: at most n/2+1 reachable states per layer, and a concrete efficiency-ratio check 88² < 365⁴.
sections.mathContext: Quantifies the O(n²) vs O(d^n) gap that makes the d=365 native_decide tractable.

sections.title: Section IX: Verified Small-d Threshold (d=7)
sections.summary: The exact k=3 threshold for d=7 is n=8, proved by native_decide (threshold_d7_lower/upper/threshold_d7).
sections.mathContext: Includes a comment with hand-confirmed R values; small d makes the unmemoized native_decide computation cheap.

sections.title: Section X: General Formula for n=3
sections.summary: Closed-form proofs: R 1 e s = e+s, R 2 (d-1) 1 = d²-1, and the general birthdayCount3 3 d = d³ - d = d(d-1)(d+1).
sections.mathContext: Among d³ functions Fin 3 → Fin d, exactly d map all three to one day; subtracting gives the max-2-per-day count d³-d. Proved by unfolding the recurrence + ring/omega.

sections.title: Section XI: Verified Threshold for d=10
sections.summary: The exact k=3 threshold for d=10 is n=12 (threshold_d10_lower/upper/threshold_d10), plus closing #check summary of the file's key results.
sections.mathContext: native_decide confirms n=12 despite the loose asymptotic prediction n≈7.5 — asymptotics are inaccurate at small d.

conclusion.summary: The slot-based recurrence reduces birthday counting from O(d^n) to O(n²). The definition is computable, the capacity theorem and polynomial bound are proved, the general n=3 formula birthdayCount3 3 d = d³ - d is proved, and thresholds for d=3,4,5,7,10,365 are all machine-verified by decide/native_decide. Fully verified: 0 axioms, 0 sorries.
conclusion.implications: The slot-based recurrence R(n, e, s) is the Lean formalization of the standard dynamic programming approach to birthday counting. The O(n²) state space is optimal: by the capacity theorem, states with n > 2e+s are unreachable, and the remaining states form a triangular region of size O(n²). This framework extends to k-way coincidences for general k by tracking a k-level histogram instead of just (e, s).
